verses.original: δὲ Ἐγένετο ἐν Ἰκονίῳ αὐτοὺς εἰσελθεῖν κατὰ τὸ αὐτὸ εἰς τὴν τῶν Ἰουδαίων συναγωγὴν καὶ λαλῆσαι οὕτως ὥστε πολὺ πλῆθος τε Ἰουδαίων καὶ Ἑλλήνων πιστεῦσαι
verses.transliteration: de Egeneto en Ikoniō autous eiselthein kata to auto eis tēn tōn Ioudaiōn synagōgēn kai lalēsai houtōs hōste poly plēthos te Ioudaiōn kai Hellēnōn pisteusai
verses.literal: - - At Iconium [Paul and Barnabas] went as usual . . . . . . into the vvv Jewish synagogue [where] they spoke so [ well ] that a great number of Jews and Greeks believed

verses.original: δὲ οἱ ἀπειθήσαντες Ἰουδαῖοι ἐπήγειραν τῶν ἐθνῶν καὶ ἐκάκωσαν τὰς ψυχὰς κατὰ τῶν ἀδελφῶν
verses.transliteration: de hoi apeithēsantes Ioudaioi epēgeiran tōn ethnōn kai ekakōsan tas psychas kata tōn adelphōn
verses.literal: But the unbelieving Jews stirred up the Gentiles and poisoned [their] minds against the brothers

verses.original: οὖν μὲν διέτριψαν ἱκανὸν χρόνον παρρησιαζόμενοι ἐπὶ τῷ Κυρίῳ τῷ μαρτυροῦντι ἐπὶ τῷ λόγῳ τῆς αὐτοῦ χάριτος διδόντι διὰ αὐτῶν τῶν χειρῶν γίνεσθαι σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα
verses.transliteration: oun men dietripsan hikanon chronon parrēsiazomenoi epi tō Kyriō tō martyrounti epi tō logō tēs autou charitos didonti dia autōn tōn cheirōn ginesthai sēmeia kai terata
verses.literal: So - [Paul and Barnabas] spent considerable time {there} speaking boldly for the Lord who affirmed . . . the message of His grace by enabling vvv vvv vvv them to perform signs and wonders

verses.original: δὲ τὸ πλῆθος τῆς πόλεως Ἐσχίσθη καὶ μὲν οἱ ἦσαν σὺν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις δὲ οἱ σὺν τοῖς ἀποστόλοις
verses.transliteration: de to plēthos tēs poleōs Eschisthē kai men hoi ēsan syn tois Ioudaiois de hoi syn tois apostolois
verses.literal: - The people of the city were divided - - [Some] sided with the Jews and [others] with the apostles

verses.original: δὲ ὡς τῶν ἐθνῶν καὶ Ἰουδαίων τε σὺν αὐτῶν τοῖς ἄρχουσιν ἐγένετο ὁρμὴ ὑβρίσαι καὶ λιθοβολῆσαι αὐτούς
verses.transliteration: de hōs tōn ethnōn kai Ioudaiōn te syn autōn tois archousin egeneto hormē hybrisai kai lithobolēsai autous
verses.literal: But when the Gentiles and Jews together with their - rulers vvv set out to mistreat and stone them

verses.original: συνιδόντες κατέφυγον εἰς τὰς τῆς Λυκαονίας πόλεις Λύστραν καὶ Δέρβην καὶ τὴν περίχωρον
verses.transliteration: synidontes katephygon eis tas tēs Lykaonias poleis Lystran kai Derbēn kai tēn perichōron
verses.literal: they found out about it and fled to the - Lycaonian cities of Lystra and Derbe and to the surrounding region

verses.original: κἀκεῖ ἦσαν εὐαγγελιζόμενοι
verses.transliteration: kakei ēsan euangelizomenoi
verses.literal: where they continued to preach the gospel

verses.original: Καί ἐν Λύστροις ἐκάθητο τις ἀνὴρ ἀδύνατος τοῖς ποσὶν χωλὸς ἐκ μητρὸς αὐτοῦ κοιλίας ὃς οὐδέποτε περιεπάτησεν
verses.transliteration: Kai en Lystrois ekathēto tis anēr adynatos tois posin chōlos ek mētros autou koilias hos oudepote periepatēsen
verses.literal: - In Lystra there sat a man crippled in [his] feet who was lame from . . . . . . birth [and] {had} never walked

verses.original: οὗτος ἤκουσεν λαλοῦντος τοῦ Παύλου ὃς ἀτενίσας αὐτῷ καὶ ἰδὼν ὅτι ἔχει πίστιν τοῦ σωθῆναι
verses.transliteration: houtos ēkousen lalountos tou Paulou hos atenisas autō kai idōn hoti echei pistin tou sōthēnai
verses.literal: This [man] was listening to the words of - Paul who looked intently at him and saw that he had faith - to be healed

verses.original: μεγάλῃ φωνῇ εἶπεν Ἀνάστηθι ὀρθός ἐπὶ σου τοὺς πόδας καὶ ἥλατο καὶ περιεπάτει
verses.transliteration: megalē phōnē eipen Anastēthi orthos epi sou tous podas kai hēlato kai periepatei
verses.literal: In a loud voice [Paul] called out Stand up on your - feet And [the man] jumped up and began to walk

verses.original: τε Οἵ ὄχλοι ἰδόντες ὃ Παῦλος ἐποίησεν ἐπῆραν αὐτῶν τὴν φωνὴν Λυκαονιστὶ λέγοντες Οἱ θεοὶ κατέβησαν πρὸς ἡμᾶς ὁμοιωθέντες ἀνθρώποις
verses.transliteration: te Hoi ochloi idontes ho Paulos epoiēsen epēran autōn tēn phōnēn Lykaonisti legontes Hoi theoi katebēsan pros hēmas homoiōthentes anthrōpois
verses.literal: [When] the crowds saw what Paul had done they lifted up their - voices in the Lycaonian language - The gods have come down to us in human form . . .

verses.original: τε Βαρνάβαν ἐκάλουν τὸν Δία δὲ τὸν Παῦλον Ἑρμῆν ἐπειδὴ αὐτὸς ἦν ὁ ἡγούμενος τοῦ λόγου
verses.transliteration: te Barnaban ekaloun ton Dia de ton Paulon Hermēn epeidē autos ēn ho hēgoumenos tou logou
verses.literal: - Barnabas they called - Zeus and - Paul [they called] Hermes because he was the chief - speaker

verses.original: τε ὅ ἱερεὺς τοῦ Διὸς τοῦ ὄντος πρὸ τῆς πόλεως ἐνέγκας ταύρους καὶ στέμματα ἐπὶ τοὺς πυλῶνας ἤθελεν θύειν σὺν τοῖς ὄχλοις
verses.transliteration: te ho hiereus tou Dios tou ontos pro tēs poleōs enenkas taurous kai stemmata epi tous pylōnas ēthelen thyein syn tois ochlois
verses.literal: - The priest - of Zeus - [whose temple] was just outside the city brought bulls and wreaths to the [city] gates hoping to offer a sacrifice along with the crowds

verses.original: δὲ οἱ ἀπόστολοι Βαρνάβας καὶ Παῦλος Ἀκούσαντες διαρρήξαντες αὐτῶν τὰ ἱμάτια ἐξεπήδησαν εἰς τὸν ὄχλον κράζοντες
verses.transliteration: de hoi apostoloi Barnabas kai Paulos Akousantes diarrēxantes autōn ta himatia exepēdēsan eis ton ochlon krazontes
verses.literal: But [when] the apostles Barnabas and Paul found out about this they tore their - clothes [and] rushed into the crowd shouting

verses.original: καὶ λέγοντες Ἄνδρες τί ποιεῖτε ταῦτα ἡμεῖς καὶ ἐσμεν ἄνθρωποι ὁμοιοπαθεῖς ὑμῖν εὐαγγελιζόμενοι ὑμᾶς ἐπιστρέφειν ἀπὸ τούτων τῶν ματαίων ἐπὶ ζῶντα θεὸν ὃς ἐποίησεν τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτοῖς
verses.transliteration: kai legontes Andres ti poieite tauta hēmeis kai esmen anthrōpoi homoiopatheis hymin euangelizomenoi hymas epistrephein apo toutōn tōn mataiōn epi zōnta theon hos epoiēsen ton ouranon kai tēn gēn kai tēn thalassan kai panta ta en autois
verses.literal: - - Men why are you doing this We too are [only] men human like you We are bringing you good news . . . that you should turn from these - worthless things to [the] living God who made - heaven and - earth and - sea and vvv everything in them

verses.original: ἐν ταῖς παρῳχημέναις γενεαῖς ὃς εἴασεν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη πορεύεσθαι αὐτῶν ταῖς ὁδοῖς
verses.transliteration: en tais parōchēmenais geneais hos eiasen panta ta ethnē poreuesthai autōn tais hodois
verses.literal: In - past generations [He] let all - nations go their [own] way

verses.original: καίτοι οὐκ ἀφῆκεν αὑτὸν ἀμάρτυρον ἀγαθουργῶν διδοὺς ὑμῖν ὑετοὺς οὐρανόθεν καὶ καρποφόρους καιροὺς ἐμπιπλῶν ὑμῶν τὰς καρδίας τροφῆς καὶ εὐφροσύνης
verses.transliteration: kaitoi ouk aphēken hauton amartyron agathourgōn didous hymin hyetous ouranothen kai karpophorous kairous empiplōn hymōn tas kardias trophēs kai euphrosynēs
verses.literal: Yet vvv He has not left Himself without testimony to His goodness He gives you rain from heaven and fruitful seasons filling your - hearts with food and gladness

verses.original: Καὶ ταῦτα λέγοντες μόλις κατέπαυσαν τοὺς ὄχλους τοῦ μὴ θύειν αὐτοῖς
verses.transliteration: Kai tauta legontes molis katepausan tous ochlous tou mē thyein autois
verses.literal: Even with these words vvv [Paul and Barnabas] could hardly stop the crowds from vvv sacrificing to them

verses.original: δὲ Ἰουδαῖοι Ἐπῆλθαν ἀπὸ Ἀντιοχείας καὶ Ἰκονίου καὶ πείσαντες τοὺς ὄχλους καὶ λιθάσαντες τὸν Παῦλον ἔσυρον ἔξω τῆς πόλεως νομίζοντες αὐτὸν τεθνηκέναι
verses.transliteration: de Ioudaioi Epēlthan apo Antiocheias kai Ikoniou kai peisantes tous ochlous kai lithasantes ton Paulon esyron exō tēs poleōs nomizontes auton tethnēkenai
verses.literal: Then [some] Jews arrived from Antioch and Iconium and won over the crowds - They stoned - Paul [and] dragged [him] outside the city presuming he was dead

verses.original: δὲ τῶν μαθητῶν κυκλωσάντων αὐτὸν ἀναστὰς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὴν πόλιν Καὶ τῇ ἐπαύριον ἐξῆλθεν σὺν τῷ Βαρνάβᾳ εἰς Δέρβην
verses.transliteration: de tōn mathētōn kyklōsantōn auton anastas eisēlthen eis tēn polin Kai tē epaurion exēlthen syn tō Barnaba eis Derbēn
verses.literal: But [after] the disciples had gathered around him he got up and went back into . . . the city And the next day he left with - Barnabas for Derbe

verses.original: τε Εὐαγγελισάμενοί ἐκείνην τὴν πόλιν καὶ μαθητεύσαντες ἱκανοὺς ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς τὴν Λύστραν καὶ εἰς Ἰκόνιον καὶ εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν
verses.transliteration: te Euangelisamenoi ekeinēn tēn polin kai mathēteusantes hikanous hypestrepsan eis tēn Lystran kai eis Ikonion kai eis Antiocheian
verses.literal: - They preached the gospel to that - city and made many disciples . . . [Then] they returned to - Lystra - - Iconium and - Antioch

verses.original: ἐπιστηρίζοντες τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν μαθητῶν παρακαλοῦντες ἐμμένειν τῇ πίστει ἡμᾶς δεῖ Διὰ πολλῶν θλίψεων εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ ὅτι
verses.transliteration: epistērizontes tas psychas tōn mathētōn parakalountes emmenein tē pistei hēmas dei Dia pollōn thlipseōn eiselthein eis tēn basileian tou Theou kai hoti
verses.literal: strengthening the souls of the disciples [and] encouraging [them] to continue in the faith We must endure many hardships to enter . . . the kingdom - of God - [they said]

verses.original: δὲ Χειροτονήσαντες πρεσβυτέρους αὐτοῖς κατ’ ἐκκλησίαν προσευξάμενοι μετὰ νηστειῶν παρέθεντο αὐτοὺς τῷ Κυρίῳ εἰς ὃν πεπιστεύκεισαν
verses.transliteration: de Cheirotonēsantes presbyterous autois kat’ ekklēsian proseuxamenoi meta nēsteiōn parethento autous tō Kyriō eis hon pepisteukeisan
verses.literal: - [Paul and Barnabas] appointed elders for them in each church praying [and] fasting as they entrusted them to the Lord in whom they had believed

verses.original: Καὶ διελθόντες τὴν Πισιδίαν ἦλθον εἰς τὴν Παμφυλίαν
verses.transliteration: Kai dielthontes tēn Pisidian ēlthon eis tēn Pamphylian
verses.literal: [After] passing through - Pisidia they came to - Pamphylia

verses.original: καὶ λαλήσαντες τὸν λόγον ἐν Πέργῃ κατέβησαν εἰς Ἀττάλειαν
verses.transliteration: kai lalēsantes ton logon en Pergē katebēsan eis Attaleian
verses.literal: And [when] they had spoken the word in Perga they went down to Attalia

verses.original: Κἀκεῖθεν ἀπέπλευσαν εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν ὅθεν ἦσαν παραδεδομένοι τῇ χάριτι τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰς τὸ ἔργον ὃ ἐπλήρωσαν
verses.transliteration: Kakeithen apepleusan eis Antiocheian hothen ēsan paradedomenoi tē chariti tou Theou eis to ergon ho eplērōsan
verses.literal: From [Attalia] they sailed to Antioch where they had been commended to the grace - of God for the work - they had just completed

verses.original: δὲ Παραγενόμενοι καὶ συναγαγόντες τὴν ἐκκλησίαν ἀνήγγελλον ὅσα ὁ Θεὸς ἐποίησεν μετ’ αὐτῶν καὶ ὅτι ἤνοιξεν θύραν πίστεως τοῖς ἔθνεσιν
verses.transliteration: de Paragenomenoi kai synagagontes tēn ekklēsian anēngellon hosa ho Theos epoiēsen met’ autōn kai hoti ēnoixen thyran pisteōs tois ethnesin
verses.literal: [When] they arrived - they gathered the church {together} [and] reported all that - God had done through them and how He had opened [the] door of faith to the Gentiles

verses.original: δὲ διέτριβον οὐκ ὀλίγον χρόνον σὺν τοῖς μαθηταῖς
verses.transliteration: de dietribon ouk oligon chronon syn tois mathētais
verses.literal: And they spent vvv a long time [there] with the disciples
